threat_assessment:
Start with the good news: you are on the table's radar from turn three, and you are going to use that. Sisay resolves on turn three in 8,028 of 10,000 seeded goldfish iterations (mean 2.96, 99.1% by turn six), so the pod sees your commander before it sees anything else. At a bracket 4 table where four Game Changers were named in the pregame conversation, nobody extends you the durdly-five-colour-goodstuff benefit of the doubt. Fine — they are watching the wrong thing.

A freshly cast Sisay is genuinely harmless, and the good players can see that too. With no other legendary permanent out she is a 2/2 whose gate reads 'mana value less than 2' — three cards in the entire deck. With zero legendary lands in the list, the mana-value-0 floor that would otherwise always be live simply isn't there. Nobody spends removal on that, and that is your head start.

The real threshold is unusually legible, and it isn't Sisay — it is colours among your OTHER legendary permanents. The ladder runs 3 / 10 / 23 / 28 / 33 fetchable targets at power 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6. The 2-to-3 colour step is the whole game: plus thirteen targets in one card, from 'pile of undersized legends' to 'toolbox that finds an answer to almost anything.'

The fifth colour is a trap for your attention. It buys combat stats and Jodah's anthem and zero new access, because nothing in this deck costs more than five. Your grace period expires at the third colour. Spend it there.

Four things flip you from ignored to archenemy, and only one of them is a card. First: five untapped colour-producing sources next to an untapped Sisay. Anyone counting mana reads that as 'activation available' — and she has no tap symbol at all, so summoning sickness never gates her, and 'she only just came down' is not the reprieve opponents assume.

Second, and louder than any legend you fetch: an omni-mana body resolving. Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Jegantha, Esika. The table knows the activation is five distinct pips with zero generic, so the body that solves that is the tell.

Third: Najeela, the Blade-Blossom, at which point you are simply the archenemy. Fourth: a second activation inside one turn cycle, which retires any remaining doubt about what the deck is.

So sequence the colours onto bodies that read fair. Katilda (1/1), Reki (1/2), Yoshimaru (1/1), Bristly Bill, Lotho — and prefer the two-colour legends, because Katilda, Kutzil, Kinnan, Lotho, Kambal and Saffi each buy two rungs on one unthreatening card.

Hold the five-pip payment until you intend to spend it. Visibly open WUBRG taxes the whole table's plays, but it also bluffs interaction you structurally cannot have — all six counterspells and both free protection instants are non-legendary and must be drawn. A tapped-out board holding a modest permanent is quieter than an open board holding nothing.

Now the deflection asymmetry, because almost no other deck gets this one: your scariest cards live in your library and you can reach them at will. Most decks must draw and hold their finisher; you never need Najeela or Jodah in hand. Play the entire midgame as a fair legends deck, stay one activation from the kill, and time the tell for the turn it wins rather than the turn it impresses.

Cheap spotlight-management is fetchable too. Loran of the Third Path's '{T}: You and target opponent each draw a card' is a political card with a body, and Kambal and Sheoldred read as hate aimed at the table's engine seat rather than at anyone in particular. Rhystic Study is the exception and the trap: it is a Game Changer, it is non-legendary — a card you drew rather than a card you chose — and it will make you the archenemy faster than anything Sisay can find. Think twice about deploying it at a table still deciding who to hit.

Now the mirror, because knowing how you die is how you sequence. The good pilots do not kill Sisay — that costs you the recast tax and the ladder, but you rebuild, and if she dies mid-activation the fetch still happens off her last known power. They kill the rung: the one legend that is the sole source of a colour, in response to the activation, so the fetch shrinks. Audit that every turn — which colour is single-sourced?

That permanent, not your commander, is the removal magnet. And Shalai, Voice of Plenty — hexproof for you and every other creature you control — is the fetch that retires the whole attack. The other way you die is a sweeper, which is doubly expensive against you: it takes the board and drops the ladder from 28 targets back to three.

Embrace the label when three conditions land together: three or more colours among your other legends, the five pips payable, and either a protection effect or Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar holding the window open. That is the pivot. Until then, be the fourth-most-interesting board at the table on purpose — you know exactly what you are building toward.

One open question worth knowing rather than acting on. Her gate reads power, not colour count, and both Flowering of the White Tree (+2/+1 on legendary creatures) and Jodah's anthem raise power — read together, the two cards say the ceiling is higher than the ladder table implies. The strategic frame keeps that in the unverified column and so should you. Nothing in the deck costs more than five anyway, so it changes nothing today.
matchups:
Sweeper control. Assume the wrath — across four players one is near-certain — and price it correctly, because against you it costs double: it takes the board and collapses the ladder from power 5 or 6 back to power 2, where exactly three cards in the deck are legal fetches and no legendary lands give you a mana-value-0 floor. The Sisay reading of 'commit only as much as wins before it arrives' is about where the colour lives, not how much of it you show. Keep a two-colour legend in HAND — Katilda, Kutzil, Kinnan, Lotho, Kambal, Saffi — because a hand copy restores two rungs after the wipe while a board copy dies with everything else.

Your instants are asymmetric in a way you should enjoy. Flawless Maneuver, Heroic Intervention and Boros Charm's 'Permanents you control gain indestructible until end of turn' beat destruction-based wraths and do nothing against exile or against Toxic Deluge's -X/-X. Your own Toxic Deluge is the copy whose timing you choose — you are the deck that recovers cheapest from a wipe it picked. The goldfish says the insurance is genuinely there: protection available in 88.4% of games, 79.8% by turn six, mean turn 2.3. Rebuild worst-first, and remember each trip through the command zone adds {2}.

Stax and tax. You are the beatdown and the role is forced — race the lock's completion, because you rarely own the long game underneath one. Five coloured pips with zero generic, activated repeatedly, is the most tax-exposed engine shape in the format: there is no generic component to pay around, so anything that raises the cost of converting mana into effects, or keeps lands tapped, hits you harder than it hits a generic ramp deck.

Recount your activations under the tax, not your cards — and recount honestly, because three of your own accelerants cannot pay the activation at all. Delighted Halfling makes mana only for legendary SPELLS and an activated ability is not a spell; Unclaimed Territory is creature-spells-only; Sol Ring makes colourless against five coloured pips. Plaza of Heroes carries the same trap and its own escape: the legendary-spell ability is dead for this purpose, but the 'add one mana of any color among legendary permanents you control' ability pays the cost fine.

Your fetchable out is Loran of the Third Path — mana value 3, live from two colours, 'When Loran enters, destroy up to one target artifact or enchantment' — with Teferi's minus-three bounce as backup. Name the piece that breaks the lock on YOU, not the scariest piece on the table.

Aggro. Roughly 120 life behind three defences means you do not race — and you are not being asked to, because your answers here are virtual rather than spent. Thalia, Heretic Cathar makes their creatures and nonbasic lands enter tapped; Sheoldred turns every opponent's draw into 2 life; Shalai hands you and your other creatures hexproof, which switches off targeted burn and drain outright; Flowering of the White Tree turns a board of 1/1 and 2/1 legends into +2/+1 blockers with ward {1}.

All four are legendary permanents at mana value 2 to 4 — inside the fetch pool from two colours onward. One activation blanks plans from three seats at once, and that is the only economical way to answer aggression in a four-player game. Pulled into a two-player race? Treat it as a subgame, spend the minimum that wins it, and keep watching the other seats.

Combo. Your whole posture inverts: hold the pips for interaction and count the table's open mana instead of advancing the ladder, because the ladder is worth nothing if the game ends before it matures. Held answers rot here too — the last profitable moment for your single Path to Exile is when the piece hits the battlefield, not later.

The structural problem is that your interaction is precisely the part Sisay cannot reach. All six counterspells, Fierce Guardianship, Flawless Maneuver, Drannith Magistrate and Grand Abolisher are non-legendary — part of the 26 cards in this list permanently outside her range. But two fetchable pieces do real work, and you reach for them before you reach for a finisher. Teferi, Time Raveler at mana value 3 ('Each opponent can cast spells only any time they could cast a sorcery') deletes instant-speed combo and instant-speed interaction in the same breath, and Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar turns off opponents' spells entirely during your turn — the closest thing this deck has to tutorable disruption.

Fair value midrange, and the other engine deck. This is where you are cleanly the control seat. Picture turn fifteen with everyone on their best draws — you like that picture, which means the inevitability is yours and you should not force early action. The toolbox out-scales a fair board and the tax shell raises their conversion cost.

So manage the pod toward the game length you win. Spend a turn or two looking boring after every visible fetch, sequence Najeela and Jodah last, and cash the deflection budget on the turn you take the window rather than the turn a fetch impresses somebody.

Graveyard hate. Mostly a blank against you, and that is worth real money at a four-player table. The deck has no recursion plan beyond Saffi Eriksdotter's sacrifice trigger, so a Bojuka Bog or a Leyline of the Void pointed at your yard is a wasted card, and any hate spent on you instead of on the reanimator seat is a gift. Just do not plan around your own graveyard either: Dauthi Voidwalker's void counters are the only piece, and like every other non-legendary card here, it has to be drawn.

cover.tagline: The tutor that widens every time it fires - and the five-pip bill that comes due every time.
cover.identity: Sisay, Weatherlight Captain is a repeatable battlefield tutor whose reach is bought in colours: she is a 2/2 plus one for each colour among your other legendary permanents, and {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} searches out any legendary permanent with mana value strictly less than her power. That makes this an access curve rather than a card curve - 3 legal targets at power 2, then 10, 23, 28 and 33 as the board picks up colours - funded by 40 lands and a small battery of bodies that can produce five distinct coloured pips at once. It is a bracket 4 (Optimized) list on contents alone: four Game Changers put the floor there independently of any combo line, and the Najeela combat loop is the closer.

how_it_wins:
Everything routes through one number, and it isn't printed on Sisay. Her power is 2 plus the count of distinct colours among your OTHER legendary permanents, and her gate is mana value strictly less than that power. Counted against the 99, the ladder runs 3 legal targets at power 2, 10 at power 3, 23 at power 4, 28 at power 5, and 33 at power 6 - every legendary permanent in the deck.

The 2-to-3 step is the biggest jump you will ever buy: thirteen new targets from one card, the moment a pile of undersized legends becomes a toolbox. And the ceiling arrives a rung early - nothing in this list exceeds mana value 5, so four distinct colours already unlocks everything. The fifth colour buys combat stats and Jodah's anthem and precisely zero new access. Don't pay for it.

Two cost facts shape every turn you play. There is no tap symbol anywhere in her ability - summoning sickness never gates her, there is no once-per-turn clause, and the only cap on activations is how many times you can produce {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}. And that cost is five coloured pips with zero generic.

Here is the trap: most of what looks like acceleration cannot pay it. Sol Ring makes {C}{C}; Delighted Halfling's coloured mana is restricted to legendary spells, and an activated ability is not a spell; Unclaimed Territory is creature-spells-only. What does pay: Command Tower, Arcane Signet, Plaza of Heroes' third mode, Secluded Courtyard named on Human, and the six-card pip battery - Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Jegantha, Esika, Relic of Legends and Selvala.

The seeded goldfish (10,000 iterations, seed 42) says Sisay herself is never the problem: mean cast turn 2.96, 99% by turn six. Assembling her alongside a five-colour source is the real curve, and that lands 55.8% of the time by turn six. Build your early turns around that assembly, not around her.

What access buys you is answers you never have to hold. The deck carries exactly one unconditional creature removal spell and one sweeper; instead it fetches taxes. Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar and Teferi, Time Raveler decide when your opponents are allowed to act at all; Thalia, Heretic Cathar makes their creatures and nonbasic lands arrive tapped; Kambal and Sheoldred convert their own spells and draws into losses. Every one of those is legendary at mana value 2 to 4 - inside the pool once the ladder reaches two or three colours.

The insurance lives there too: Shalai, Voice of Plenty, Flowering of the White Tree, and Plaza of Heroes in the mana base, available 80% of the time by turn six on the goldfish. Then Ioreth, Samut, Emiel and Seedborn Muse turn one activation per turn into several by untapping the battery.

The kill is Najeela, the Blade-Blossom, and this manual promises you exactly one version of it. The Najeela plus Derevi combat loop is the single line in this deck that has been resolved against the Comprehensive Rules and passed an adversarial check - a genuine, deterministic, unbounded combat loop that kills the table, though not the self-contained two-card infinite the combo data advertises. Nine other lines the combo data flags for this deck - Najeela with Faeburrow Elder, with Esika, with Selvala, the Emiel blink loops, the Ioreth-Samut-Selvala mana line, the five-card Jegantha line - are unverified here. Play them as board states you may stumble into, not as plans.

Watch where the fourth colour comes from. Among the 33 other legendary permanents, white appears on 19 and green on 14, but blue on only 8, red on 6 and black on 5 - and the only red source at mana value 3 or less is Najeela herself. The colour that finishes your ladder and the card that makes you the archenemy are frequently the same card.

The honest weakness is structural. Twenty-six of the 99 are not legendary and therefore permanently outside the tutor's reach: three of the six cards that can pay her activation (Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Relic of Legends), all six counterspells, both free protection instants, and all four Game Changers. Sisay finds payoffs - she does not find her own fuel or her own protection. That is why the bracket floor holds at 4 no matter what happens to the combo lines (four Game Changers is already over bracket 3's cap of three), and it is why the mulligan section below is about enablers rather than about her.

card_roles.Sisay, Weatherlight Captain: Your engine and your clock. She is a 2/2 plus one for each colour among your OTHER legendary permanents, and {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} finds any legendary permanent with mana value strictly less than her power - 3 targets at power 2, 10 at 3, 23 at 4, 28 at 5, 33 at 6. No tap symbol, no once-per-turn clause: the only limit on activations is producing five distinct pips again.
card_roles.An Offer You Can't Refuse: One mana stops the noncreature spell that would end the game, at the price of two Treasures handed back. Non-legendary like every counterspell here, so you draw it, never fetch it - spend it on a win attempt, not a value engine.
card_roles.Arcane Denial: Two mana counters anything and pays its controller two cards for the trouble. The cheapest catch-all in a six-counterspell suite Sisay is structurally blind to.
card_roles.Arcane Signet: One of the few rocks that actually pays her: any colour in your commander's identity means all five, unrestricted. It ramps toward Sisay and covers a pip of her activation.
card_roles.Birds of Paradise: One mana, any colour, no strings attached - the cleanest single pip in the deck. One of the cards that turns a turn-two Sisay into a turn-three activation.
card_roles.Bloom Tender: The best card in the pip battery: one mana of each colour among permanents you control, scaling on exactly the resource the ladder scales on. It is not legendary, so she can never find it - this card's absence is the deck's fuel problem in one line.
card_roles.Boros Charm: You are here for the middle mode: permanents you control gain indestructible, which saves the ladder along with the board. Four damage to a face is the mode for someone who is already dead.
card_roles.Bristly Bill, Spine Sower: A two-mana green rung that grows the team on every land drop. Cheap colour-diverse bodies are how you climb from power 2 to power 4 without showing the table anything worth killing.
card_roles.Dauthi Voidwalker: Shadow makes it effectively unblockable in most pods, it exiles everything your opponents would put in a graveyard, and it can sacrifice to cast one of those cards for free. Non-legendary - a drawn clock, not a fetched one.
card_roles.Delighted Halfling: It ramps Sisay out early and makes her uncounterable on the way down - then cannot pay a single pip of her activation, because that mana is restricted to legendary spells and an activated ability is not a spell. Know which half of the card you are holding.
card_roles.Derevi, Empyrial Tactician: Three colours on one mana-value-3 card: she alone takes Sisay from 2/2 to 5/5 and the pool from 3 cards to 28, then taps or untaps a permanent every time one of your creatures connects. She is also the verified half of the deck's kill - her command-zone ability is inert here, and she starts in the library.
card_roles.Dihada, Binder of Wills: Three colours and a planeswalker on one card. The +2 is genuine commander insurance - vigilance, lifelink and indestructible on Sisay until your next turn - and the -3 digs specifically for legendary cards.
card_roles.Dispel: One mana answers the removal spell or counterspell aimed at your activation window. The narrowest card in the deck and often the most relevant - hold it, don't plan around it.
card_roles.Drannith Magistrate: A Game Changer and one of the four cards holding this deck's bracket floor at 4. Opponents casting only from hand blanks command zones, graveyards and exile-cast combo pieces at once - and it is non-legendary, so drawn only.
card_roles.Emiel the Blessed: A {3} blink outlet: re-buy Loran's artifact kill, Derevi's tap-or-untap, or Shalai's arrival. The value use is real; the Emiel blink loops the combo data flags for this deck are unverified, so don't treat them as a plan.
card_roles.Esika, God of the Tree // The Prismatic: The front face gives every other legendary creature you control '{T}: Add one mana of any color' - your fetched board becomes the mana base. Note the front face is mono-green: it adds exactly one colour to Sisay's power despite the five-colour back.
card_roles.Esper Sentinel: A one-mana tax on the table's first noncreature spell each turn: they pay, or you draw. Non-legendary, so it comes off the top of your deck rather than out of the middle.
card_roles.Faeburrow Elder: The battery's other half - it grows with each colour among your permanents and taps for one of each of those colours. Also not legendary: the engine needs it and cannot go looking for it.
card_roles.Fellwar Stone: Coloured mana off your opponents' lands - unreliable in principle, unrestricted in practice, which is more than Sol Ring can say about paying a five-pip cost.
card_roles.Fierce Guardianship: Free while you control a commander, which here is nearly always. A Game Changer and part of the bracket floor; non-legendary, so it is drawn insurance rather than a fetchable plan.
card_roles.Flawless Maneuver: Costs nothing with a commander out and protects the whole board - which is what matters, because the wrath that kills your creatures also collapses the ladder from power 5 back to power 2.
card_roles.Flowering of the White Tree: Ward {1} on every legendary creature is the cheapest standing tax on removal aimed at Sisay, and the +2/+1 raises her power - the exact number the fetch gate reads.
card_roles.Grand Abolisher: During your turn nobody casts a spell or activates an artifact, creature or enchantment ability - your activation turn becomes untouchable. Non-legendary: Sisay cannot find her own best protection.
card_roles.Heliod, Sun-Crowned: A white rung that is indestructible and awkward to answer, converting your lifegain into +1/+1 counters and handing out lifelink on demand.
card_roles.Heroic Intervention: Hexproof and indestructible for every permanent you control - one card against both disasters at once, the removal spell aimed at Sisay and the sweeper that resets the ladder.
card_roles.Ioreth of the Healing House: Untaps two other legendary creatures for a single tap: the battery's refuel button, and a blue rung at mana value 3.
card_roles.Jegantha, the Wellspring: One tap for {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} - the entire activation from one permanent. Mana value 5 means power 6 and four colours before Sisay can find it, and the companion clause is inert in this list, since Flowering of the White Tree carries two of the same symbol.
card_roles.Jodah, the Unifier: The ceiling target at mana value 5: power 6, four distinct colours. He repays it with an anthem on your legendary creatures and a free legendary spell whenever you cast one from hand - note 'cast', which the permanents Sisay puts onto the battlefield are not.
card_roles.Kambal, Consul of Allocation: Two colours at mana value 3 plus a standing drain on every noncreature spell in the pod. The black half is structurally scarce: only five of the deck's 33 other legendary permanents supply black at all.
card_roles.Katilda, Dawnhart Prime: Two colours for two mana, plus a mana ability for every Human you control - Sisay included, who is a Human Soldier with no tap symbol on her activation, so she can tap for {W} and still fire.
card_roles.Kenrith, the Returned King: A five-mana sink with an ability in every colour, including graveyard recursion for the whole table's benefit and yours. Mono-white on the ladder and mana value 5, so power 6 before she can fetch him.
card_roles.Kinnan, Bonder Prodigy: Two colours for two mana, and every time you tap a nonland permanent for mana he adds one more of a type that permanent just produced - a free extra pip off Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Jegantha or a Treasure, every single tap.
card_roles.Kodama of the West Tree: A green rung that turns any modified creature connecting into a basic land from your library - the deck's only repeatable land ramp - and hands trample to the counters this deck keeps accumulating.
card_roles.Kutzil, Malamet Exemplar: Two colours at mana value 3 and the tax that matters most here: opponents cannot cast spells during your turn, so every future activation becomes a window they are not allowed to answer.
card_roles.Loran of the Third Path: The only artifact or enchantment answer in the deck stapled to a legendary body - the only one Sisay can go and get. This is the card you fetch at the stax seat.
card_roles.Lotho, Corrupt Shirriff: Two colours for two mana and a Treasure off every player's second spell each turn - instant-speed fixing the activation can actually spend, and one of only two black sources at mana value 3 or less.
card_roles.Mikaeus, the Lunarch: One of only three legendary permanents under mana value 2, so one of the three cards a cold-start Sisay can find. He is {X}{W} and a fetched card is not cast; whether he arrives as a 0/0 is flagged for a stack scenario, so don't build a turn on him.
card_roles.Mox Amber: The deck's only mana-value-0 rung and the cheapest fetch available - but it is colourless, so it adds no colour to Sisay's power, and its mana depends on legendary creatures and planeswalkers you already control.
card_roles.Najeela, the Blade-Blossom: The finisher, and the only source of red at mana value 3 or less - so the colour that completes your ladder and the card that makes you the archenemy are often the same card. Her untap-attackers ability costs exactly what Sisay's does, so the pip battery double-duties.
card_roles.Negate: Two mana for the noncreature spell you cannot let resolve. Non-legendary - drawn, not fetched.
card_roles.Path to Exile: Your one unconditional answer to a creature. Against a combo seat, the last profitable moment to spend it is when the piece hits the battlefield - not later.
card_roles.Raff Capashen, Ship's Mage: Two colours at mana value 4 and flash on every historic spell: develop the ladder on an end step while representing interaction all the way around the table.
card_roles.Reki, the History of Kamigawa: A green rung that draws a card for each legendary spell you cast. Note 'cast' - the permanents Sisay puts onto the battlefield do not trigger him, so Reki rewards the cards in your hand, not the ones on the ladder.
card_roles.Relic of Legends: Taps any untapped legendary creature you control for a colour of your choice - the cheapest converter from fetched board to activation mana. Not legendary, so she cannot find it, and whether a legend that arrived this turn can be tapped for it is an open question flagged for a stack scenario.
card_roles.Rhystic Study: A Game Changer and one of the four cards fixing the bracket floor at 4. Also non-legendary: the deck's best draw engine is one Sisay can never look for.
card_roles.Rona, Herald of Invasion // Rona, Tolari: A two-mana blue rung that untaps whenever you cast a legendary spell and loots while it waits, with a late transform if the game stalls out.
card_roles.Saffi Eriksdotter: Two colours for two mana plus a sacrifice that returns a creature put into your graveyard this turn. Whether that can rescue Sisay herself turns on declining the command-zone replacement - flagged for a stack scenario.
card_roles.Samut, Voice of Dissent: Flash, double strike, and the line that matters: other creatures you control have haste - the blanket answer to every 'it only just arrived' problem a fetched creature has.
card_roles.Seedborn Muse: A Game Changer, and in a deck whose engine is an activated ability, close to the best card in it: untapping all your permanents during each opponent's untap step means one activation per player per turn cycle. Non-legendary, so she must be drawn.
card_roles.Selvala, Heart of the Wilds: A green rung at mana value 3 whose {G} and a tap become X mana in any combination of colours, X being your largest creature's power - with a five-power body on board, that is the full {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} in one activation.
card_roles.Shalai, Voice of Plenty: Hexproof for you and every other creature you control: one permanent answers 'kill her on sight' and 'shrink her power in response' at the same time. She does not protect herself, so fetch her before you need her.
card_roles.Sheoldred, the Apocalypse: A black rung at mana value 4 that taxes the whole table's card draw and refills your life total. Black is the deck's scarcest ladder colour, supplied by only five of the 33 other legendary permanents.
card_roles.Silence: One white mana buys the turn outright. A pivot-turn card - hold it for the activation you intend to win with, not the one that merely looks impressive.
card_roles.Sol Ring: The fastest route to a turn-two Sisay and completely useless for paying her: {C}{C} covers none of a five-pip cost with zero generic. It accelerates the commander, not the engine.
card_roles.Surrak Dragonclaw: Three colours on one card at mana value 5, a 6/6 with flash, and your creature spells cannot be countered - relevant to the legends you cast from hand, since the ones Sisay puts onto the battlefield were never counterable to begin with.
card_roles.Swan Song: One mana stops an enchantment, instant or sorcery. The 2/2 flier you hand back is rarely the problem at a table where the problem was the spell.
card_roles.Teferi, Time Raveler: Two colours at mana value 3 and a static that reduces the whole table to sorcery speed: no instant-speed removal in response to an activation, no counterspell on your turn.
card_roles.Thalia, Heretic Cathar: A white rung that makes every creature and nonbasic land your opponents play enter tapped - a tax on three seats at once, which is how this deck does removal.
card_roles.Toxic Deluge: The sweeper whose timing you choose, priced in life so it scales to any board. You rebuild cheapest afterwards - provided you kept a colour-diverse legend in hand rather than committing it.
card_roles.Yoshimaru, Ever Faithful: One of the three cards a power-2 Sisay can find, and the one that actually steps the ladder - a white body that grows with every legendary permanent that follows it.
card_roles.Command Tower: Any colour in your commander's identity, unrestricted - for Sisay that is any of the five pips. One of the two lands the verified Najeela loop leans on.
card_roles.City of Brass: Any colour for one damage. In the verified combat loop it never needs to be tapped at all - activating a mana ability is never mandatory - so treat that damage as a choice you are making, not a cost you are owed.
card_roles.Mana Confluence: Any colour for one life; City of Brass's untapped twin. Same note: the loop's floor is zero life, and this is one of the two lands you skip to get there.
card_roles.Exotic Orchard: Any colour a land an opponent controls could produce - in a four-player pod, usually most of them. Read the table before you count it as your fifth pip.
card_roles.Plaza of Heroes: Three modes matter: colourless, a legendary-spell-only colour, and the important one - any colour among legendary permanents you control, unrestricted mana the activation can spend. The exile mode gives a legendary creature hexproof and indestructible: commander insurance living in your mana base.
card_roles.Forbidden Orchard: Any colour, at the price of handing an opponent a 1/1 Spirit each time you tap it. Sequence it on turns where a surprise blocker cannot cost you a race.
card_roles.Secluded Courtyard: Name Human. Its coloured mana may be spent to activate an ability of a creature source of the chosen type, and Sisay is a Human Soldier - so unlike Unclaimed Territory, this land genuinely pays for her activation.
card_roles.Unclaimed Territory: Name Human to deploy your legends - but the coloured mana is restricted to creature spells only, so it can never pay one pip of Sisay's ability. One of three accelerants in this deck that are dead to its own commander.
card_roles.Breeding Pool: Pay the two life. Five distinct pips with no generic filler means a land entering tapped on the turn you wanted to activate costs far more than two life.
card_roles.Godless Shrine: Untapped white and black on demand - and black is the scarcest colour on this ladder, supplied by only five of your legendary permanents.
card_roles.Hallowed Fountain: White and blue on demand: the fixing behind Teferi, Raff and the entire counterspell shell.
card_roles.Overgrown Tomb: Black and green - the colour the ladder is thinnest in, paired with the one it is richest in.
card_roles.Sacred Foundry: Red and white. Red appears on only six of your 33 other legendary permanents, so this is frequently the land that supplies the {R} pip.
card_roles.Steam Vents: Blue and red - the two colours a board-based five-pip payment most often lacks.
card_roles.Stomping Ground: Red and green: the Jegantha, Samut and Surrak end of the curve, and a red source that is not Najeela.
card_roles.Temple Garden: Green and white, the deck's densest pair - Katilda, Kutzil, Saffi, Derevi, Emiel and Shalai all draw on it.
card_roles.Watery Grave: Blue and black, the two thinnest colours among your legendary permanents. Worth the two life every time.
card_roles.Bountiful Promenade: Untapped green and white in any real pod - two or more opponents means no tempo cost and no life paid.
card_roles.Luxury Suite: Untapped black and red with two or more opponents: free access to the deck's two scarcest ladder colours.
card_roles.Rejuvenating Springs: Untapped green and blue in a multiplayer pod, with no life paid for the privilege.
card_roles.Sea of Clouds: Untapped white and blue with two or more opponents - a free dual for the Teferi and Raff half of the deck.
card_roles.Spectator Seating: Untapped red and white in a pod, and one more red source that does not require you to reveal Najeela.
card_roles.Spire Garden: Untapped red and green with two or more opponents - the painless Stomping Ground.
card_roles.Undergrowth Stadium: Untapped black and green in a pod - the scarce colour paired with the abundant one, for free.
card_roles.Vault of Champions: Untapped white and black with two or more opponents, feeding Lotho, Kambal and Sheoldred.
card_roles.Arid Mesa: Finds Sacred Foundry, Stomping Ground or a basic Mountain or Plains. One life for exactly the pip you are missing is the right price in a deck whose signature cost has no generic component.
card_roles.Flooded Strand: Finds Hallowed Fountain, Breeding Pool or a basic Plains or Island - the fetch you crack when the fourth pip is blue.
card_roles.Marsh Flats: Finds Godless Shrine, Watery Grave or a basic Plains or Swamp - the cheapest access to the deck's scarcest colour.
card_roles.Misty Rainforest: Finds Breeding Pool, Hallowed Fountain or a basic Forest or Island: green and blue on one life.
card_roles.Polluted Delta: Finds Watery Grave, Godless Shrine or a basic Island or Swamp - the two thinnest colours on the ladder in one card.
card_roles.Scalding Tarn: Finds Steam Vents, Breeding Pool or a basic Island or Mountain: blue and red for one life.
card_roles.Verdant Catacombs: Finds Overgrown Tomb, Watery Grave or a basic Forest or Swamp - the black pip most often comes from here.
card_roles.Windswept Heath: Finds Temple Garden, Sacred Foundry or a basic Forest or Plains - the deck's densest colour pair.
card_roles.Wooded Foothills: Finds Stomping Ground, Sacred Foundry or a basic Mountain or Forest: the red pip without the Najeela tell.
card_roles.Plains: One white pip that no Blood Moon, Wasteland or Thalia tax can complicate. White is your most abundant colour, so this is the basic you fetch last.
card_roles.Island: One blue pip, uncastable-proof. Blue appears on only eight of your other legendary permanents, so a basic Island is a real fetch target rather than a formality.
card_roles.Swamp: One black pip in the deck's scarcest colour - five of 33 legendary permanents supply black, so this basic gets fetched more often than its count suggests.
card_roles.Mountain: One red pip. Six legendary permanents supply red and one of them is Najeela, so a basic Mountain is sometimes how you complete a five-colour payment without showing your hand.
card_roles.Forest: One green pip for the deck's second-densest colour, and the fetch target when Bloom Tender or Selvala is the card you actually need to cast.

mulligan:
Mulligan for enablers, not payoffs. The reason sits in the decklist: 26 of the 99 are not legendary and are invisible to Sisay forever - including three of the six cards that can pay her activation (Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Relic of Legends), all six counterspells, and all four Game Changers. She finds payoffs; she does not find fuel or protection. A hand of Sisay plus three expensive legends does nothing until you draw the enabler yourself.

The seeded model keeps 84.2% of first sevens on a simple two-to-five-lands rule and mulligans a mean of 0.183 times per game. Translation: your opening hands are usually fine on lands, and the judgement is all colour and fuel.

Three things make a keep. First, two to four lands with at least one unrestricted colour source - Command Tower, City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Exotic Orchard, Plaza of Heroes, Forbidden Orchard, a fetch land, or Secluded Courtyard on Human. Second, something that pays or accelerates: Birds of Paradise, Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder, Arcane Signet, Fellwar Stone, Relic of Legends. An early accelerant is there 63.8% of the time by turn six at a mean of turn 2.8, so a hand without one is not unlucky - it is below curve.

Third, and best of all, a cheap two-colour legend. Katilda, Kinnan, Lotho, Saffi, Kambal and Kutzil each buy two ladder rungs for two or three mana, and Derevi buys three for three.

Now ship the payoff hands. A seven with Jodah, Kenrith, Surrak, Samut or Jegantha and no fixing is four uncastable cards and a 2/2 commander whose gate reads 'mana value less than 2' - three legal targets, one of them colourless. Ship the hand whose only acceleration is Sol Ring plus Delighted Halfling: both put Sisay down a turn early, and neither can pay one pip of what she does there. Ship the counterspells-and-a-land seven - interaction is the half of the deck you can afford to draw into later.

And be honest about the mana. Five coloured pips with zero generic sits off the end of the standard colour-source tables, so a hand with four lands that make three colours between them is a hand that casts your commander and then stares at her.

Two sequencing notes belong in the decision. You are keeping toward the ladder's second rung, not toward a turn-three Sisay - the model already casts her by turn three in 8,028 of 10,000 games. And a cold-start activation is worse than it looks: at power 2 the three legal targets are Mox Amber, Mikaeus and Yoshimaru, of which Mox Amber is colourless and steps the ladder not at all, and Mikaeus's behaviour when fetched rather than cast is an open question. Land a colour-diverse legend first, then activate.
upgrades:
The ten below come from a single question asked ten times: can the engine find it? There is no sideboard here, so every name is scouted from the wider pool, and the pool was screened the way this deck spends - against a five-pip activation and a tutor that only sees legendary permanents. Seven of the ten pass that second test outright: legendary, Sisay-fetchable, led by Gaea's Cradle and Minamo, School at Water's Edge - mana-value-0 legendary lands in a list that runs zero, which makes them live fetches even for a cold-start Sisay at base power 2. The other three each convert cards already sleeved into a named combo line.

Read the evidence tiers the way I do. Every combo line an entry opens is flagged 'needs a stack scenario' - promising, not proven, and priced accordingly. EDHREC rank tells you adoption, the Game Changer flag tells you what the pregame conversation will sound like, and the bracket column reads 4 before and 4 after on all ten: the floor does not move, so none of these is a power-level decision in disguise.

The screen's rejections tell you as much as its picks. Freed from the Real opens eight lines but is non-legendary and dead without a drawn dork - exactly the blind spot the deck already suffers. Basalt Monolith feeds the Kinnan line colourless mana, which a {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} activation cannot spend. And every obsolescence-index 'upgrade' over Faeburrow Elder fails the same oracle read - none makes multicoloured mana toward the five-pip activation - which is why none of them made the ten.
mana_base:
Forty lands, and 17 of them enter tapped — 42%, over the one-in-three budget the deck builder allows itself. In most decks that's a tempo tax you shrug off. In a deck whose signature cost is five distinct pips untapped at once, it's the first number I watch. Underneath it the colour spread is deliberately flat: 15 white land sources, 14 green, 12 each in blue, black and red.

Flat sources against unflat pips is the interesting disagreement. White carries 38.3% of the deck's pips on 23.1% of the sources; red carries 8% of the pips on 18.5%. Nine of the 40 lands are fetches, which count as sources of nothing here — that's why a 40-land deck only ever reads 12 to 15 per colour. The gap is the activation talking: the base is priced for {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, which wants all five colours at once no matter what the cast costs say.

Black is the weak leg, and the number is stark. On lands alone you have black on curve 29.9% of the time. What sets the bar that high is a double-black cost priced at turn two — Dauthi Voidwalker's {B}{B} — which pushes black's target to 36 sources against the 12 in the lands. The ramp is the answer: it lifts black to 61% on curve and the source count to 21.

That ramp package is 16 pieces — nine dorks, five rocks, a ritual and one land-ramp effect — and it's what makes the rest of the table read comfortably. With rocks and dorks counted, green sits at 95.1% on curve, white at 94.4%, blue at 90.7%, red at 89.5%. Raw mana crosses the activation's five on turn six: mean 5.869, up from 3.187 on turn three. After that, colour is your constraint, never count.

One accounting note that matters here more than anywhere: the tables count only unconditional mana. Delighted Halfling and Unclaimed Territory make mana that cannot pay an activated ability at all, so a five-pip activation can't touch it — they count as coloured sources of nothing. Plaza of Heroes keeps one unrestricted coloured mode, and Secluded Courtyard says "or activate an ability", so read the clause, not the phrase. What sits beside this prose is the price of your real engine, not your best-case draw.

combo_lines.002:
The combo data pleads Najeela, the Blade-Blossom plus Derevi, Empyrial Tactician as a two-card infinite, and cites it toward this deck's bracket 4 floor. Stack 002 tried that claim step by step against the Comprehensive Rules, through three checker passes. The holding: partially accurate - which is worth more to you at a table than a yes would have been.

Savour the operative clause first: mana pools empty at every step change. Najeela and Derevi produce no mana between them, so 'self-contained' fails - each iteration's {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} must be raised again from scratch. What survives is better than the claim: the loop is real, deterministic, unbounded, and it kills the table.

The funding arithmetic is the arithmetic of attackers. Untapping the attackers and adding a combat phase means the next combat declares everything again, and every attacker except Derevi is a Warrior who makes one more token, so attackers follow A' = 2A - 1: three, five, nine, seventeen, thirty-three. Derevi's triggers equal the number of creatures connecting while Najeela's cost stays fixed at five - so combat 1 yields only three triggers and must be pre-funded from your untapped lands, combat 2 breaks exactly even at five, and combat 3 runs away with nine. Damage per combat is A + 3 - six, eight, twelve, twenty - and the first defending player dies during combat 4.

One further correction, and it is worth money: the loop's life cost is 0, not 2. Command Tower covers {B} through Sisay's five-colour identity, and Plaza of Heroes' third mode covers W, U, R and G off the colours Najeela and Derevi already put on the battlefield - five taps needing only three Plaza untaps, which combat 1's three Derevi triggers supply exactly. City of Brass and Mana Confluence never have to be tapped at all, because activating a mana ability is never mandatory; the two life per combat you will hear quoted is the naive line that taps all five lands, not a floor. For the record: both halves are mana value 3, so both come off a Sisay at power 4 - two colours among your other legends - and Derevi is a three-colour card who gets you most of the way there by herself.
